newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico bought 100,000 T Brazil soybeans - USB.
newsitem.headline: Mexico bought 100,000 T Brazil soybeans - USB.

text.p: Mexico bought 100,000 tonnes of Brazilian soybeans through Veracruz port, the United Soybean Board (USB) said in a recent report.
It cited unconfirmed reports that the four vessels of beans were bought at $20 less than the price of U.S. soybeans at the time.

A high level of Brazilian exports recently should make Brazilian beans scarce for the rest of the year, the USB said. A drop in the price of U.S. beans should also make Brazilian soybeans less attractive, it added.

"Also, the bean tariff for non trade agreement (NAFTA) countries goes in to effect in August, which makes it doubly difficult for the Brazilians to offer beans to Mexico for the rest of the marketing year," the report said.
The entry of Brazilian beans to Mexico was expected to drag down domestic prices.
Mid-bridge Laredo prices for soybeans at the Texas-Mexico border fell to $295 per tonne on July 1, from $331 per tonne on June 13.
